counterevidence_considered.description: The closest candidate for repeated unit entry is that 100 berries were collected per block, which could in principle have yielded many sub-block measurements per unit. However, the description states the berries were pooled into a single composite before extraction, producing exactly one anthocyanin value per block, so no within-block replicates ever enter the row-independent procedure.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: 100 berries per block pooled to a single composite value before assay

evidence.description: All 24 data rows in data/input.csv carry distinct block_id values (BLK-01 through BLK-24), so the declared independent unit appears exactly once per row and no unit enters the two-sample test more than once. Group counts are 12 vsp and 12 sprawl, matching the report.

The workflow explicitly enforces uniqueness of the independent-unit column before any analysis: it raises a ValueError if block_id does not uniquely identify each row, so a repeated unit could not silently enter the Welch t-test.
evidence.observed_value: uniqueness guard present and would abort on duplicate block_id

evidence.description: The data description states that the file is already at the independent-unit level: one row per independently owned and managed block, with block_id named as the independent unit column, and each code appearing on exactly one row.
evidence.observed_value: row = one block; block_id declared as independent unit; one code per row

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one independently owned and managed Syrah vineyard block, summarized by the single 100-berry composite sample collected in that block on its harvest day
Independent unit column: block_id

- `block_id`: the survey code for the vineyard block, for example BLK-07. Each
  code appears on exactly one row; there are as many rows as blocks.

evidence.description: The report's selected result is a Welch two-sample t-test on the 24 block-level values, and its claim that rows correspond one-to-one with independent blocks matches the data. The reported group means (1.514 and 1.236 mg/g, n = 12 each) reproduce from the raw column values.

source_refs.quoted_text: The file records 24 Syrah vineyard blocks, each at a different estate and each trained on a single trellis system. Each block contributes exactly one analyzed row: a 100-berry composite drawn across the block at harvest and assayed once. Rows therefore correspond one-to-one with independent blocks, and no block appears twice.

[selected-result] Welch two-sample t-test on 24 independent vineyard blocks (12 vertical shoot positioning, 12 sprawl): mean berry skin anthocyanin was 1.514 mg/g under vertical shoot positioning versus 1.236 mg/g under sprawl, a difference of 0.278 mg/g (t = 4.99, df = 20.86, p < 0.001); anthocyanin was higher under vertical shoot positioning.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by (1) scanning all 24 block_id values in data/input.csv for duplicates — none exist, and every identifier BLK-01 through BLK-24 appears exactly once; (2) checking whether the workflow could aggregate or expand rows so that a block contributes more than one value to the t-test — collect() pulls exactly one anthocyanin value per row and read_blocks() aborts on duplicate block_id, so it cannot; (3) looking for sub-unit replication (multiple berries or point-quadrat insertions per block) entering the test — both were pooled or averaged to a single block-level value in the field before the file was created; and (4) recomputing group counts and means from the raw column, which match the report (12/12, 1.514 vs 1.236 mg/g). No path by which an independent unit enters the procedure more than once was found.
